brief: `applyLight`'s dusk wash is `clamp(1 - |hour - 19|/1.8)` - a hard-coded hour inside a light term. It reads 0.53 at a midwinter dusk and 0.00 at a midsummer one, so the town's evening light is warmest on the wrong evenings and absent on the longest ones. #112 fixed the MORNING half of exactly this fault onto `sunUp` and left the evening; `dawnF()`/`dawnEdge()` are the shape to mirror, keyed on `sunDown` rather than a constant. Why now: sky is 6 back, this is a measured seasonal bug invisible to any single screenshot, and it is the last hard-coded hour in the light.
successLooksLike: The evening warmth peaks at the same offset from sunset in every season - print the wash's value at sunset+k for k over a year and show a flat line where there was a 0.53-to-0.00 swing. A midsummer dusk visibly warms where it previously did nothing. Filmstrip 0 POP through the whole evening on both a midwinter and a midsummer day.
avoid: If b140 has landed, re-measure the dusk wash on HEAD before changing it - the building shadows change the frame's light at exactly this hour and the number you are correcting may have moved. Do not touch the morning half; it is already correct and byte-identical work is not the brief. `day` rolls at hour 6, so an evening term must not index off a counter that has already turned over.
